BiblicalUsage: The word names fainting, being disconsolate, and Job uses it once, for the afflicted man who needs pity from his friend. To him that is afflicted pity should be shown, Job says, even though he has forsaken the fear of the Almighty.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the fainting man deserves pity before he deserves a lecture, and Job's friends failed him the moment they chose argument over compassion.
